verdict_scope: Original derived support for unnumbered logarithmic necessity assertion; not exact source theorem/proof reproduction or a source repair.

seven_slots.name: objects_and_spaces
seven_slots.source: Scalar predictions and outcomes in [0,1]; full revealed past; static interval comparator.
seven_slots.lean: Real predictions with pointwise interval terminal premise; Boolean vectors mapped to 0/1; measurable seeded policies on full newest-first Boolean histories.
seven_slots.delta: Binary paths are valid restricted adversaries sufficient for a lower bound on the interval game. General interval-history learner restriction is a mathematical specialization; no named real-history/randomized-kernel representation theorem was audited.

seven_slots.name: quantifier_order
seven_slots.source: Unavoidable logarithmic dependence without a displayed quantified lower theorem.
seven_slots.lean: For every measurable seed space, probability law and measurable-section globally interval-valued policy, and every positive natural T, there exists one length-T Boolean vector with the expected regret bound.
seven_slots.delta: Concrete finite-horizon completion, not a transcription. Witness depends on policy, law and T, never on the realized seed. No path hard for every policy, nor one infinite path hard at all horizons.

seven_slots.name: assumptions
seven_slots.source: Interval actions/outcomes and causal play; positive horizon implicit. Lower randomization regularity unspecified.
seven_slots.lean: MeasurableSpace Omega, IsProbabilityMeasure mu, each seed section measurable, every seed/history action in [0,1], T>0.
seven_slots.delta: Measurability/probability specify the selected expected-regret contract. Pointwise global range matches valid actions in this explicit contract. No nonmeasurable or almost-everywhere-only policy equivalence is asserted. No concentration, variance or regret lower bound is a terminal premise.

seven_slots.name: conclusion_metric
seven_slots.source: Cumulative squared learner loss minus minimum cumulative loss of one fixed hindsight comparator. Lower rate asserted in prose.
seven_slots.lean: Same-path learner loss minus empirical-mean loss. binary_mean_minimizer and imported mean APIs establish feasible interval minimization for positive T.
seven_slots.delta: Exact source regret metric on binary data, with a new finite expected-regret lower theorem. Not pseudo-regret, dynamic regret, loss alone or a surrogate. The source iid min outside expectation is not confused with realized hindsight regret.

seven_slots.name: constants_normalization
seven_slots.source: No lower constant or offset. 4+4 ln T belongs exclusively to FTL upper theorem. No half-factor or horizon averaging.
seven_slots.delta: Original derived non-sharp constants and offsets, not source-printed values or exact minimax value. Their order supports logarithmic necessity. Source upper harmonic comparison is not used as a lower proof.

seven_slots.name: probability_feedback
seven_slots.source: Full outcome revelation and causal decisions. Expectation removal qualified by determinism. Post-prediction adversary discussion concerns upper bound.
seven_slots.lean: Seed plus strict-past outcomes determine actions. Finite path law is independent of learner/seed. Final fixed path lies outside seed integral. Integrability derived from measurable sections and absolute regret <=T.
seven_slots.delta: Precise randomized expected-regret extension. No seed-dependent adverse path, high-probability/seedwise guarantee, bandit feedback or infinite filtration assertion. Finite sums and integral interchange suffice; no conditional-distribution axiom is needed for this statement.

seven_slots.name: boundary
seven_slots.source: Lower proof and formal specification omitted; vector and absolute-loss exercises separate.
seven_slots.lean: Finite positive horizon, Boolean adverse outcomes, pointwise bounded measurable seeded policies, static empirical comparator.
seven_slots.delta: At T=0 regret is zero but proposed bounds positive, so positive horizon necessary. No sharp minimax, abstract-all-randomization representation, all-horizon hard path, whole-chapter completion or source-proof reproduction.
